title: Prospective Shadow-Mode Evaluation of a Clinical Surveillance and Alert System for the Detection of Critical Findings and Potential Treatment Gaps
summary:
This study evaluates a clinical surveillance and alert system designed to automatically identify critical findings and potential gaps in care from existing routine clinical data. The system jointly evaluates laboratory results, vital signs, medication data, pre-existing diagnoses, diagnoses documented during the course of treatment, allergies, and findings from diagnostic imaging. It is intended to detect both individual critical findings, such as severely abnormal laboratory values or relevant imaging findings, and cross-source clinical constellations that may indicate a potential treatment gap.

The study is conducted prospectively in shadow mode. This means that the system operates during routine clinical care and generates internal alerts, but these alerts are not communicated to the treating teams. They do not influence diagnostic procedures, treatment, or other clinical decisions. No additional examinations or interventions are performed.

The study aims to determine how reliably, completely, and rapidly the system identifies relevant findings and constellations. Only data collected or documented as part of routine care are analyzed. Data processing takes place within the Charité infrastructure. Identifiable primary data may only be accessed by Charité staff.
conditions: Critical clinical findings and potential treatment gaps in adult intensive care patients.

interventions.name: The observational cohort comprises adult patients treated in one of the participating intensive care units during the study period. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age ≥ 18 years
- Treatment in one of the participating intensive care units WD1i, WD2i, M101i, M102i, or M103i at Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin
- Stay in a participating unit during the study period from 10 October 2026 to 1 March 2027
- Availability of data collected or documented as part of routine care in at least one of the investigated data categories
Exclusion criteria:
No additional study-specific exclusion criteria. Any exclusions resulting from data protection requirements, consent requirements, or objections will be governed by the ethics approval and the approved data protection concept.
